subject: Model fit & safety evals - post-call and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Emily Chen <emily.chen@healthscope.com>, Jason Lee <jason.lee@healthscope.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model fit & safety evals - post-call and next steps

Hi Emily / Jason —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same plan: 

Recap from discovery call:
- Primary use case: triage assistant for intake nurses and clinicians (symptom prompting + suggested next steps).
- Volume: ~2k requests/day initially, spiking to 10k for pilot; latency target: median <200ms for short responses.
- Sensitivity: outputs may reference PHI; refusal/safety behavior for out-of-scope medical advice is critical.

Recommended evaluation plan (what Redwood will deliver):
1) Sandbox access to a dedicated model endpoint with example prompt sets (2 business days access).
2) Pre-populated prompt set and benchmark suite (attached): healthscope_prompt_set_v1.jsonl + benchmarks spreadsheet.
3) Two candidate models for initial fit: rw-instruct-v2-medium (better instruction following) and rw-llama-q4f16-v1 (cost-optimized with quantization). We recommend rw-instruct-v2-medium for safety/guardrail fidelity, rw-llama-q4f16-v1 as a low-cost variant for throughput testing.
4) Safety/refusal evals: we will run your prompt sets against both models and provide a short report on refusal rates, hallucination examples, and policy-triggered outputs. We will also include a small suite of domain-sensitive prompts (suicide/medication/dx requests) to validate guardrails.

Action items / next steps:
- Emily/Jason: confirm that sandbox access is ok and let us know two people to provision (email addresses).
- Redwood: provide sandbox link + attach prompt set + benchmarks (attached).
- Redwood Security (cc Rafael as SE): will follow up on PHI/data retention questions and provide the security one-pager.
- Schedule: propose follow-up in one week to review benchmark results (suggest Thurs 10/28 AM PT).

Attachments: healthscope_prompt_set_v1.jsonl, healthscope_benchmarks_20261021.xlsx

If that looks right I’ll provision the sandbox today.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Jason Lee <jason.lee@healthscope.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dr. Emily Chen <emily.chen@healthscope.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit & safety evals - post-call and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and aligned with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Can you confirm whether PHI will be logged in the sandbox environment? We need to ensure no persistent logs contain identifiable patient data.
- For safety/refusal, can you share examples of the guardrail prompts you plan to use (we want to ensure they don't over-refuse in borderline cases)?
- Timeline: if we get access today, when can we expect the initial benchmark report?

Also looping Procurement on timeline for pilot contracting.

Thanks,
Jason
Sr. Product Manager, Clinical Systems
HealthScope

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@healthscope.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit & safety evals - post-call and next steps

Hi Jason / team —

Looping in from Security/Compliance. Short answers and what we can provide immediately: 

- Sandbox logging: the sandbox endpoint runs in an ephemeral environment by default; we can disable persistence for payloads that contain PHI. For evaluation we recommend token/metadata logging off — if you need request tracing we can provide hashed request IDs that are non-reversible.
- Data retention & KMS: we support customer-managed keys (KMS) for all dedicated/private environments; for hosted sandbox we can provide short-term encrypted ephemeral keys and a 7-day retention window that can be shortened. We can also sign a narrow DPA addendum for the pilot.
- Guardrails & refusal prompts: our safety team will share the guardrail prompt set (redwood_safety_refusals_v1) and a short doc explaining thresholds. That set is editable and we can tune the sensitivity per your feedback.
- Evidence & attestations: we can attach our SOC 2 Type II summary and the one-pager (attached). If you need deeper artifacts (penetration test reports / architecture diagram) we can schedule an NDA-sharing package.

Next steps from Security:
1) Marissa — confirm who at HealthScope to provision for sandbox (emails).
2) Jason/Emily — send any sample PHI redaction rules you use (we can mirror in prompt preprocessing).
3) Redwood — provide guardrail prompts + short refusal examples; Rafael to run initial tests with your prompt set and report refusal/hallucination metrics.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you want to go deeper on PHI handling.

-Rishi
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Model fit & safety evals - post-call and next steps

Thanks Jason — and thanks Rishi for the clear answers.

Confirming next steps and timelines (we’ll action today):
- Sandbox provisioning: I will provision a 48-hour sandbox and disable persistent logging for the accounts below. Please confirm these two provisioning emails for access: jason.lee@healthscope.com, emily.chen@healthscope.com
- Attachments: attaching the prompt set (healthscope_prompt_set_v1.jsonl), benchmarks spreadsheet (healthscope_benchmarks_20261021.xlsx), and security one-pager (redwood_security_onepager.pdf). Rafael will run the prompt set against the two candidate models and deliver an initial bench + safety summary within 48 hours of sandbox activation.
- Timeline: sandbox activation later today (EOD PT). Initial benchmark & safety report by Fri 10/23 EOD PT. Follow-up review call Thurs 10/28 or Fri 10/29 (I’ll send a calendar poll).
- Items for HealthScope: please share any PHI-redaction rules (email or doc) and confirm the two provisioning emails. Procurement: let us know if you need a PO or SOW to proceed with pilot provisioning.

Rafael / Priyom — Rafael will own running the model fit tests and the safety/refusal checks; Priyom will help with prompt-tuning and producing the sample prompt variants.

Thanks all — excited to get this moving.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
